source_user: Advanced cluster case cluster scheduling and recovery-6: Design a resilient cluster scheduler for distributed LLM training and inference. Variant 6 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: cover gang scheduling, GPU/NIC/topology-aware placement, fragmentation, preemption, checkpoint cadence, node drain, elastic restart, replica routing, SLOs, and resource accounting. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat scheduler behavior as a measured control-plane hypothesis, not as proof of resilience. Assumptions: jobs declare GPU, CPU, memory, storage, network/NIC, topology, parallelism, checkpoint size, and priority needs; node/GPU/NIC inventories and failure semantics are observable; DP/TP jobs can restart from a consistent checkpoint, while platform-specific capacities and SLOs must be measured.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 6: topology-aware gang admission plus checkpoint-aware preemption and bounded node-drain recovery reduces failed/restarted training work without violating inference SLOs, compared with the current first-fit scheduler. Hold workload mix, cluster inventory, model, checkpoint policy, and routing policy constant; run matched canary periods and inject a controlled node loss. A result supports the hypothesis only if p95 training recovery time and wasted GPU-hours improve with confidence intervals and no SLO regression; otherwise reject the change.

Design: maintain an inventory with GPU model/count, free memory, PCIe/NVLink, NIC, NUMA, RDMA fabric, and topology labels. Admit distributed training as a gang, reserve compatible GPU/NIC/topology sets atomically, and avoid fragmentation with backfill only for jobs that fit without breaking reservations. Use preemption by priority and checkpoint age, with grace periods and quotas; do not evict protected inference replicas. Drain a failing or suspect node, fence it before reuse, checkpoint at a measured cadence, restart the training gang with the same placement constraints or an explicitly supported elastic policy, and route inference replicas away from unhealthy capacity with readiness checks.

Measure admission and queue time (s), allocated versus requested GPU-hours, fragmentation (% stranded capacity), preemption count and lost work (steps and GB), checkpoint duration/size (s/GB), restart and recovery time (s), node-drain time (s), training throughput (tokens/s), RDMA/NIC errors and bandwidth (Gb/s), replica availability, request p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), error rate, and deadline/SLO violations. Compare topology-aware versus baseline placement, record workload, world size, DP/TP mapping, topology, failure injection timing, and synchronized clocks; report medians, tail percentiles, sample counts, and confidence intervals. Confounders include workload burstiness, checkpoint storage contention, fabric congestion, heterogeneous GPUs, correlated node failures, and warm-cache effects.

Safety and rollback: deploy to a canary queue, use least-privilege scheduler and node-agent permissions, preserve audit logs without credentials, and cap concurrent preemptions. Roll back to the prior scheduler if recovery p95 exceeds the baseline by 10%, inference p99 latency or error SLO regresses, checkpoint corruption occurs, or stranded capacity rises by 15% for two observation windows. Quiesce new admissions, restore prior placement/routing policy, validate checkpoints, and drain/recover only through an approved, reversible procedure. Evidence required before claiming improvement: inventory/topology snapshots, scheduler decisions, failure-injection records, checkpoint integrity checks, per-job traces, resource accounting, and matched baseline results.

node fencing, preemption, or elastic restart can cause data loss or unsafe duplicate work if not coordinated
evidence_required: versioned scheduler and node-agent configuration

Use preemption by priority and checkpoint age, with grace periods and quotas; do not evict protected inference replicas. Drain a failing or suspect node, fence it before reuse, checkpoint at a measured cadence, restart the training gang with the same placement constraints or an explicitly supported elastic policy, and route inference replicas away from unhealthy capacity with readiness checks.

Compare topology-aware versus baseline placement, record workload, world size, DP/TP mapping, topology, failure injection timing, and synchronized clocks; report medians, tail percentiles, sample counts, and confidence intervals. Confounders include workload burstiness, checkpoint storage contention, fabric congestion, heterogeneous GPUs, correlated node failures, and warm-cache effects.

Safety and rollback: deploy to a canary queue, use least-privilege scheduler and node-agent permissions, preserve audit logs without credentials, and cap concurrent preemptions. Roll back to the prior scheduler if recovery p95 exceeds the baseline by 10%, inference p99 latency or error SLO regresses, checkpoint corruption occurs, or stranded capacity rises by 15% for two observation windows. Quiesce new admissions, restore prior placement/routing policy, validate checkpoints, and drain/recover only through an approved, reversible procedure. Evidence required before claiming improvement: inventory/topology snapshots, scheduler decisions, failure-injection records, checkpoint integrity checks, per-job traces, resource accounting, and matched baseline results.
